newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF head says he did not make comments on dollar.
newsitem.headline: MOF head says he did not make comments on dollar.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday that he had not made any comments earlier this week on the future yen/dollar exchange rate while in the United States for the G7 and IMF meetings.
"I did not refer to how the dollar should move in the future at all," he said at a Tokyo briefing upon his return from the U.S. trip.

Kubo said in New York that he favoured a strong dollar but not necessarily a stronger one. Some players in the financial markets had interpreted his remarks as a signal on Japan's foreign exchange rate policy.
On Tuesday, a finance ministry official said Kubo's comments on a "strong" dollar did not mean the Japanese government was opposed to a stronger dollar.
Kubo said on Wednesday finance ministers of the Group of Seven industrialised countries agreed to welcome recent currency moves.
"U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in Washington that the U.S. supports a strong dollar, but I don't think he was saying that the U.S. will seek a stronger dollar," Kubo said.
